failure_summary.description: Skill has no guidance for exposing an 'executable function contract' derived from a schema input model via the repo's Fn(...)/implementSync(...) pattern; agent only produced the schema class and a plain function, missing the Fn contract wrapper entirely.

patch.reasoning: The single trajectory shows the agent correctly modeled the input as an S.Class (schema law followed) but had no rule telling it that when a task asks for an 'executable function contract' over a schema input, the repo convention is a schema-derived Fn(...) definition wired to the implementation via .implementSync(...)/.implement(...), with the plain function re-exported as a thin call-through. Because this rule is entirely absent, the agent invented its own plain-function shape instead. Adding one Fast Rule (plus a workflow classification hook) closes this gap without hardcoding the fixture's specific names.

edits.target:
- Prefer `MappedLiteralKit` when a protocol/code mapping needs both encoded and
  decoded literal helper surfaces.
edits.content:
- When a task asks for a schema-owned input model plus an "executable function
  contract" (not just a plain helper function), model the contract itself as a
  schema-derived `Fn(...)` value built from the input/output schemas, and wire
  the real implementation with `.implementSync(...)` (or the async variant) —
  do not hand-write a bare function as the sole export when the task names a
  distinct input schema and a distinct function-contract export.
